 WACO, Texas (KXXV) — A former Waco middle school teacher pleaded guilty in federal court for laundering more than $500,000 of stolen federal tax refunds, according to the U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Texas, Justin R. Simmons. 
 Court documents revealed that Jeremy Jarod Jackson, a former teacher at G.W. Carver Middle School, admitted to posing as a trustee of the SWBC Professional Employee Service and changing the business address to send direct tax refunds to himself. 
 He obtained checks totaling $520,000, depositing the money into his accounts for personal expenses. 
 According to court documents, an IRS Criminal Investigation special agent prevent Jackson from depositing more than $4 million in stolen refund checks into his accounts. 
 Jackson faces up to 10 years in prison for one count of money laundering.
